chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Dawood Al-Raqqi, who said:

I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) at Mina when a man came and said, 'A group of people arrived on the day of the sacrifice, and they have missed the Hajj.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'We ask Allah for health, and I see that each one of them should spill the blood of a sheep, and they should be freed from the Ihram, and upon them is the Hajj in the future if they return to their lands; and if they stay until the days of Al-Tashreeq in Makkah, then they should go out to a juncture of the people of Makkah and enter into Ihram from it, and perform Umrah, so there would not be upon them the Hajj in the future.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who misses Hajj on the Day of Sacrifice?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific fidya (expiation) of sacrificing a sheep for those who missed the core Hajj rites on Yawm al-Nahr, highlighting the Imam’s pragmatic distinction between returning home versus staying in Mecca. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the obligation of Hajj is tied to the ability to perform the complete ritual, offering a clear path for immediate rectification through Umrah if one remains in the holy city during the days of Tashreeq. This ruling reflects the flexibility within the Shia school regarding the timing of Hajj obligations when circumstances prevent timely completion.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said,

‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> at Mina when a man came over, so he said, ‘A group of people arrived on the day of the sacrifice, and they have missed the Hajj’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for the health, and I<sup>asws</sup> see that each one of them should spill blood of a sheep, and they should be freeing from the Ihraam, and upon them is the Hajj in the future if they leave to go to their cities; and if they stay until the days of Al-Tashreek (11<sup>th</sup>, 12<sup>th</sup> and 13<sup>th</sup> of Zilhajj) in Makkah, then they should go out to a juncture of the people of Makkah and wear their Ihraam from it, and they should perform Umra, so there would not be upon them the Hajj in the future’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Dawud al-Riqqiy who has said the following:

“Once I was with abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in Mina 5 when a man came and asked about a people who arrived on the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering) and they had missed their Hajj. He (the Imam) said, ‘We ask well-being from Allah and I say that every one of them must slaughter one sheep and come out of the state of Ihram. They owe Hajj in future if they go home. If they wait in Makkah until the days of Tashriq (11, 12 and 13 of Dhu al-Hajjah) are over, then go out to Miqat (place for assuming the state of Ihram) of the people of Makkah, assume the state of Ihram to perform al-‘Umrah, then they will not owe any Hajj in future. ‘“
